hints.title: Adjacent Identical Character Obstacle
hints.text: If any character appears more than (len(s) + 1) // 2 times, no valid rearrangement exists. How can placing the most frequent remaining characters greedily prevent collisions?

hints.title: Max-Frequency Greedy Invariant
hints.text: Always pick the character with highest remaining count that differs from the previous placed character. Track characters in a max-priority queue.

hints.title: Priority Queue Interleaving Procedure
hints.text: Build a frequency table. If any count > (len(s) + 1) // 2, return empty string. Place counts into a max-priority queue. While queue has >= 2 elements, pop the two most frequent characters, append both to result, decrement counts, and push back if positive. Handle any final single character.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of string s (1 <= N <= 500)
complexity.notes: Greedy priority queue interleaving popping top 2 frequent characters with alphabet size at most 26.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating permutations takes O(N!) time which is impossible for N up to 500.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Heap size bounded by alphabet size 26.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Checking the pigeonhole impossibility condition max_freq > (len(s) + 1) // 2 upfront.

solutions.approach: Greedy priority queue interleaving of most frequent characters
